"""TSV cell sanitizer."""
from typing import Optional

def sanitize_cell(text: Optional[str]) -> str:
    if text is None:
        return r"\N"  # Rule H10: None/null values serialized as \N

    # Rule H10: Backslash escaping convention for internal audit logs.
    # Order of replacement matters: escape backslashes first, then other special characters.
    # This prevents newly introduced escape backslashes from being re-escaped.
    sanitized = text.replace(r"\\", r"\\\\")  # Escape backslashes first
    sanitized = sanitized.replace('"', r'\"')  # Escape double quotes with backslash
    sanitized = sanitized.replace('\n', r'\n')  # Escape newlines with \n
    sanitized = sanitized.replace('\t', r'\t')  # Escape tabs with \t (implied by H10 as delimiter)

    return sanitized

def requires_sanitization(text: str) -> bool:
    # This function is not directly used by exporter.py in the current context,
    # but its logic would align with the full set of characters needing escaping.
    return any(c in text for c in ('\t', '\n', '"', '\\'))
